name: Macher Jhol
instructions: 1. Clean and marinate fish pieces with salt and 1/2 teaspoon turmeric.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan and shallow fry the fish pieces until golden; remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, fry the potato wedges until lightly browned and set aside.
4. Add nigella seeds and slit green chilies to the remaining oil until they splutter.
5. Mix ginger paste, turmeric, and chili powder with a little water and add to the pan; sauté for a minute.
6. Add the potatoes and sufficient water to create a thin gravy, then bring to a boil.
7. Gently add the fried fish to the curry and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the fish is tender.
8. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: Macher Jhol is a staple dish in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, reflecting the significant Bengali influence in the region. Due to the abundance of fresh seafood in the islands, this light curry is a beloved household meal, prized for its simplicity and the cooling properties of its thin, spice-infused broth, perfect for the tropical climate.
